description: Changes in interest rates directly affect current accounting values for assets held at fair value/mark-to-market.
Interest rates contain five elements: risk-free rate, and four other components.

To reflect the uncertainty of both cash flows and the prevailing interest rate environment, and consequent price volatility, the market requires a premium or spread over the risk-free rate to cover duration risk.
Even if the underlying instrument were risk-free, the interest rate may contain a premium to represent the market appetite for investments and the presence of willing buyers and sellers.
This is distinct from idiosyncratic credit spread, and represents the credit risk premium required by market participants for a given credit quality.
